Federal buildings within division still subject to federal EO. Hmm, but the equality map notes bans are state-level; federal EO on "government-funded single-sex facilities" — ambiguous scope (bathrooms? shelters? prisons?).

Also national risk assessment flagged 4 states Do Not Travel for trans people — not this one (it's most protective).

I'd score division around 0.60-0.68. Rule 12 says territory under restrictive parent must sit materially below comparable independent jurisdictions lacking it, but can be above parent. Parent ~0.38; division substantially higher given documented visitor-facing protections (public accommodation verified by referendum, hate crime reporting machinery, shield law, most-protective ranking, no state facility ban, X markers climate).

Between 0.60 and 0.70. The national exposures (visa screening, federal facility rule, custody) are real but the visitor-facing daily sphere in this division is protected. Also unenforced sodomy statute — tangential, dead letter (since 1974 ruling), documented.

Calibration: 0.65 anchors lack universal unremedied rules... but here the universal rules are national. The division cannot escape national entry screening. Yet note the entry screening exposure primarily affects visa applicants with document discrepancies — a trans visitor with a passport matching their gender... foreign passports issued by their own country; the cable targets discrepancies in applicant's documents/records "casting reasonable doubt on the applicant's sex" — so a visibly trans traveler whose documents suggest a different sex could be refused. That's a real entry exposure for the whole country.

I'll go 0.62. Or maybe 0.65? The division's protections are unusually strong and documented with enforcement (67.8% referendum, vote records, shield law, hate crime reporting unit). But per rule 12, must be materially below an independent comparable jurisdiction. A 0.65 anchor like Avalet (no parent regime) — division with parent regime should be at or below that. I'd say 0.60.
